title: Pasqal Coordinates Q-PLANET to Develop Chips for Neutral-Atom Quantum Tech
key_facts: Pasqal (Nasdaq: PSQL), a neutral-atom quantum computing company, coordinates Q-PLANET, co-funded by the EU Chips Joint Undertaking and national and regional authorities
Backed by 50 million euros over three years; 28 partners from 11 European countries
Will develop chip-based lasers at four wavelengths, atom chips for sensing and computing, and microfabricated vapor cells for atomic clocks and field sensors
Pasqal leads the 1013 nm chip-laser work and acts as end user of the lasers and vapor cells
Aims at standardized design kits (PDKs and ADKs) from lab to factory
Pasqal CTO Loic Henriet: three months after the Brussels kick-off the project has moved from ambition to execution
Text is a company press release carried by The Quantum Insider
quote_evidence: Backed by 50 million euros over three years, the consortium brings together 28 partners from 11 European countries.
Three months after our kick-off in Brussels, Q-PLANET has moved from ambition to execution, said Pasqal CTO Loic Henriet.
why_it_matters_hint: A publicly funded European pilot line for parts that neutral-atom quantum machines depend on.
event_date: 2026-10-06 (project kicked off about three months earlier)
